results.title: ECON 212 – Introduction to Game Theory Winter 2023

Game  theory  is  a  mathematical  language  of  modern  economic  and  social  science.  Any  time  a  model involves conflict of interest game theory is needed since it is the study of strategic  decision making. Game theory has numerous applications in economic theory, political  science,  evolutionary  biology,  computer  science,  etc.This is an introductory course, covering the foundations of game theory as well as giving  insights into some of its present-­‐day applications. The course presents main ideas and  techniques of game-­‐theoretic analysis. The aim is to teach students to use game theoretic  approach, to think strategically. Success with this course gives edge both in deeper  understanding of economic theory and in tackling some computer science problems. research.summary: The gathered materials provide a robust foundation for designing a 4-unit introductory course on game theory. Syllabi from multiple institutions (e.g., [L3oRewRFT], [aLZBsuFk5], [ZZGgu1UUW], [0bFZZPnJ8], [hBntm0Jml]) consistently emphasize a core structure covering normal-form games (strategies, payoffs, Nash equilibrium, mixed strategies) and extensive-form games (game trees, backward induction, subgame-perfect equilibrium). Advanced topics frequently included are repeated games (folk theorems), Bayesian games (incomplete information), and cooperative games (Shapley value, core). Popular textbooks identified across these courses include 'Games of Strategy' by Dixit, Skeath, and McAdams [HLwt6GyuP, q55DJ3P0N], 'Game Theory for Applied Economists' by Gibbons [L3oRewRFT, 0bFZZPnJ8], and 'Essentials of Game Theory' by Leyton-Brown and Shoham [aLZBsuFk5, ZZGgu1UUW]. Pedagogical approaches often combine formal mathematical modeling with interactive elements, such as online lab exercises (MobLab [L3oRewRFT]), in-class games [ZZGgu1UUW, q55DJ3P0N], and problem sets that focus on applying concepts to real-world scenarios like auctions, oligopoly models (Cournot/Bertrand), and bargaining. Mathematical prerequisites generally range from college-level algebra to mathematical maturity involving proofs, calculus, and probability [aLZBsuFk5, ZZGgu1UUW, hBntm0Jml].
